nucleus.thesis: Work topology determines optimal location; the false binary dissolves when teams diagnose actual dependencies rather than impose ideology.

claims.text: Synchronous and asynchronous work modes have genuine, measurable requirements. Co-location and distribution serve different topologies—neither is universally superior.
The real failure is using location as a proxy for accountability instead of building transparent feedback systems that expose actual work dependencies.
Adaptive infrastructure must match location to work type dynamically—some sprints co-locate, others distribute—without conflating attendance with loyalty or capability.
Systems thinking beats location dogmatism, but only when it includes honest diagnosis of dependency graphs rather than hiding behind both/and paralysis.
The question 'remote vs. office' is malformed. The diagnostic question is: 'What does this team's actual work topology demand, and why?'

shell.topic: Is remote work better than in-office for software teams?
